title: Private Deployment: Ops Command Center — compact status, escalation & cost context
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a condensed Operations Command Center view for Private/VPC deployments that combines cluster health, network reachability, active rollouts, and cost exposure into a single surface for SREs and platform owners. This ticket covers prototype, interaction spec, and review artifacts for the console panel that sits alongside the existing Cluster Overview.
background: Customers running Redwood Private asked for a single-pane operational surface that reduces context switching during incidents. Existing cluster pages are too modal and require jumping between Network, Upgrade, and Billing tabs. This design aims to summarize critical signals with quick escalation paths and lightweight drill-ins.
goals: Create a compact, scannable status strip for each tenant/cluster showing health, connectivity, recent upgrades, and cost anomaly flags
Provide instant escalation actions (create incident, page on-call, rollback rollout) from the same surface
Surface estimated per-hour cost pressure and the dominant driver (eg. burst GPU, long seq lengths, >X requests/min)
Design for responsive layouts so the command center works at desktop widths and tablet-sized operator consoles
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype with desktop and tablet variants linked from this ticket
Interaction spec for drill-in (click-through to Network, Upgrades, Rollouts, Billing) with keyboard shortcuts documented
Engineering feasibility review completed and trade-offs captured (render cost, telemetry requirements)
PM sign-off on escalation wording and recommended default actions
Usability notes from 3 SRE/Platform interviews included
design_notes: Primary row items: cluster name, health pill (ok/warning/critical), network reachability icon, active rollout badge, cost delta % badge
Health pill aggregates: node availability, 95p latency, recent errors — hover expands to small sparkline and top error class
Network icon shows last successful inter-region ping and active VPC peering status; clicking opens a connection health modal
Cost delta uses 24h baseline and highlights the top cost contributor with a tooltip showing estimated token-level vs infra-level split
Rollout badge expands to a tiny timeline with canary size and time-to-complete; offer quick rollback CTA when >1 canary step failed
Escalation menu (three-dot) includes: Create Incident (links to PagerDuty/Gen AI assistant), Page On-Call, Open Runbook, Start Safe-Rollback
Compact mode collapses secondary badges into an overflow menu while keeping health and cost visible
decisions: Use color + icon for health rather than numeric score to speed scanability (agreed 2025-01-20 design review)
Default to showing 'cost delta' rather than absolute cost to avoid noisy dollar estimates; PM requested link to billing for absolute numbers (2025-01-27)
Keep escalation actions externalized as configurable integrations (PagerDuty, Slack, MS Teams) — Engineering requires an abstractions layer before hard-wiring (2025-02-03)
No auto-remediation controls in first iteration; MVP will only provide manual rollback and runbook links to avoid accidental mass changes
next_steps: Address Eng feedback from 2025-02-04: reduce telemetry payload by sending aggregated 1m metrics instead of per-request samples
Prototype accessibility updates (contrast and focus order) per accessibility review scheduled 2025-02-14
Capture mapping of rollout states -> allowed quick actions and send to PM for final wording approval
Prepare handoff package (tokens: Figma frames, interaction spec, component list, telemetry spec) for ENG spike
dependencies: PM-221 (billing: cost-delta endpoint and top-contributor classification)
ENG-4105 (network: VPC reachability probe and peering health checks)
